items.title: Text block
items.prompt: Declare `String text` as a **text block** holding the two lines `Hello` and `World`, ending with a line break (put the closing `"""` on its own line).
items.hint: The opening `"""` must be followed by a new line.
items.explanation: A text block starts with `"""` and a line break. The common indentation is stripped, and a closing `"""` on its own line adds the final line break. Indentation doesn't matter for the check.

items.title: Reverse with StringBuilder
items.prompt: Given `String word`, declare `String reversed` holding `word` backwards. Use a `StringBuilder` in one statement.
items.explanation: `StringBuilder.reverse()` changes the builder in place and returns it, so the calls chain; `toString()` turns it back into a `String`.

items.title: strip and upper case
items.prompt: Given `String raw`, declare `String clean`: `raw` without leading and trailing whitespace (use the Unicode-aware method), in upper case.
items.explanation: `strip()` removes all Unicode whitespace; the older `trim()` only removes characters up to `U+0020`, so it would leave the em space in this test.

items.title: Parse to a primitive
items.prompt: Convert `String s` to a primitive `int n` with the `Integer` method that returns a primitive (not a wrapper).
items.explanation: `Integer.parseInt` returns an `int`; `Integer.valueOf` returns an `Integer` (a cached wrapper for -128 to 127). Both throw `NumberFormatException` for bad input.

items.title: char arithmetic
items.prompt: Given `char c`, declare `char next` holding the following letter. `c + 1` is an `int`, so cast it.
items.explanation: Adding to a `char` promotes it to `int`. The cast must wrap the whole sum: `(char) c + 1` would still be an `int`.

items.title: Switch expression
items.prompt: Assign `String type` from `int day` with a switch **expression** using arrow labels: 6 and 7 give `"weekend"`, anything else `"weekday"`.
items.explanation: Arrow labels never fall through, one `case` can list several constants, and a switch expression over an `int` needs `default`. Don't forget the `;` after the closing brace: it's an assignment.

items.title: Labeled break
items.prompt: Search `int[][] grid` for `target` with two enhanced `for` loops. Label the outer loop `outer`, set the existing `boolean found` to `true` and leave **both** loops when you find it.
items.explanation: A label goes right before the loop it names. `break outer;` exits the labeled loop, not just the innermost one.

items.title: yield from a block
items.prompt: Assign `int score` from `String grade` with a switch expression: `"A"` gives 4, `"B"` gives 3, and any other grade prints `unknown grade` and yields 0 (use a block with `yield`).
items.explanation: A block on the right of `->` must end by producing a value with `yield` (or throwing). `return` isn't allowed inside a switch expression.

items.title: do-while
items.prompt: With a `do`/`while` loop, print `n`, then halve it with `n /= 2`, repeating while `n > 0`. `int n` is already declared.
items.explanation: A `do`/`while` body always runs at least once, and the statement ends with a semicolon after the condition.

items.title: continue
items.prompt: Print the numbers 1 to 10 except multiples of 3, using a classic `for` loop with `int i` and `continue`.
items.explanation: `continue` skips the rest of the body and goes on with the update (`i++`) and the condition.

items.title: Record with a compact constructor
items.prompt: Declare `record Point(int x, int y)` with a **compact** constructor that throws `new IllegalArgumentException()` (no message) when `x` or `y` is negative.
items.explanation: A compact constructor has no parameter list; it sees the parameters and the fields are assigned automatically after its body runs.

items.title: Varargs
items.prompt: Write `static int sum(int... nums)` that returns the total of its arguments using an enhanced `for` loop.
items.explanation: Inside the method a varargs parameter is an ordinary array. Calling `sum()` with no arguments passes an empty array, not `null`.

items.title: Constructor chaining
items.prompt: Class `Box` already has fields `int w, h` and a constructor `Box(int w, int h)`. Add a constructor `Box(int side)` that delegates to it to make a square.
items.explanation: `this(...)` calls another constructor of the same class and must be the first statement.

items.title: Static counter
items.prompt: Declare `class Widget` with a `static int created` field and a no-argument constructor that counts every new `Widget`.
items.explanation: A static field belongs to the class, so all instances share one counter. Static fields default to `0`.

items.title: var with generics
items.prompt: Declare a local variable `names` with `var`, initialized to a new empty `ArrayList` of `String`.
items.hint: The diamond `<>` has nothing to infer from here.
items.explanation: With `var` the type comes from the right side, so the type argument must be written there. `var names = new ArrayList<>();` would infer `ArrayList<Object>`.

items.title: Switch over a sealed type
items.prompt: Write `static double area(Shape s)` returning a switch expression over the sealed `Shape`: a `Circle` (component `r`) gives `Math.PI * r * r`, a `Square` (component `side`) gives `side * side`. Use patterns and no `default`.
items.explanation: Because `Shape` is sealed and every permitted subtype has a case, the switch is exhaustive without `default`. Type patterns (`Circle c`) and record patterns (`Circle(double r)`) both work.

items.title: Functional interface
items.prompt: Declare `interface Validator`, annotated with `@FunctionalInterface`, with one abstract method `boolean isValid(String s)`.
items.explanation: A functional interface has exactly one abstract method, so a lambda can implement it. The annotation is optional but makes the compiler check that rule.

items.title: Enum with a constructor
items.prompt: Declare `enum Planet` with constants `MERCURY(3.7)` and `EARTH(9.8)`, a `final double gravity` field and a constructor that sets it.
items.explanation: Enum constants come first and end with `;` when more members follow. Enum constructors are always private (writing `private` is optional), and each constant's arguments go to the constructor.

items.title: Pattern matching for instanceof
items.prompt: Given `Object o`, write an `if` that binds `String s` with pattern matching when `o` is a `String` longer than 3 characters, and then prints `s.toUpperCase()`.
solutions: if (o instanceof String s && s.length() > 3) System.out.println(s.toUpperCase());
items.explanation: The pattern variable `s` is in scope on the right of `&&` and inside the body, where the match is known to have succeeded.

items.title: Override with @Override
items.prompt: Write `class Dog` extending the abstract class `Animal` and overriding its package-private `String sound()` to return `"Woof"`. Mark it with `@Override`.
items.explanation: An override may keep or widen the access level (package-private, `protected` or `public`), never narrow it. `@Override` makes the compiler check that a method is really overridden.

items.title: Default method
items.prompt: Declare `interface Greeter` with an abstract `String name()` and a default method `String greet()` that returns `"Hi " + name()`.
items.explanation: A default method has a body and can call the interface's abstract methods. With only one abstract method left, `Greeter` is still a functional interface.

items.title: Custom checked exception
items.prompt: Declare a **checked** exception `InsufficientFundsException` with a constructor taking `String message` that passes it to the superclass.
items.explanation: Extending `Exception` (but not `RuntimeException`) makes an exception checked. `super(message)` stores the text that `getMessage()` returns.

items.title: Multi-catch
items.prompt: Call `parse(text)` and print the result. With **one** multi-catch, print `bad input` for a `NumberFormatException` or a `NullPointerException`.
items.explanation: Alternatives are separated by `|` and share one (implicitly final) variable. They may not be subclasses of each other.

items.title: Two resources and finally
items.prompt: Open `Res a = new Res("A")` and then `Res b = new Res("B")` in one try-with-resources header, print `body` inside, and print `finally` in a `finally` block.
items.explanation: Resources close in reverse order (B, then A) right after the body, **before** `catch` and `finally` run.
items.output:
body
close B
close A
finally

items.title: Throwing an exception
items.prompt: Write `static void check(int age)` that throws `new IllegalArgumentException("age < 0")` when `age` is negative.
items.explanation: `IllegalArgumentException` is unchecked, so `check` needs no `throws` clause.

items.title: catch and finally
items.prompt: Call `risky()`. Catch any `Exception` and print `"failed: "` plus its message; always print `cleanup` in a `finally` block.
items.explanation: `finally` runs whether or not an exception was thrown or caught.

items.title: Comparator chain
items.prompt: Sort `List<Person> people` in place by `age()`, then by `name()`, using `Comparator.comparing` (or `comparingInt`) and `thenComparing` with method references.
items.explanation: `thenComparing` breaks ties of the first comparator. `List.sort` and `Collections.sort` both sort in place.

items.title: Counting with merge
items.prompt: Count each word of `String[] words` into the existing `Map<String, Integer> counts` using a for-each loop and `merge`.
items.explanation: `merge(key, 1, Integer::sum)` puts `1` for a new key and otherwise combines the old value with `1`.

items.title: 2D array
items.prompt: Declare `int[][] grid` with 3 rows and 4 columns (all zeros), then set the last cell of the last row to 9.
items.explanation: `new int[3][4]` creates 3 row arrays of 4 zeros. Indexes start at 0, so the last cell is `[2][3]`.

items.title: Deque as a stack
items.prompt: Declare `Deque<Integer> stack` as a new `ArrayDeque`, push 1, 2 and 3, then print `stack.pop()`.
items.explanation: `push` and `pop` work at the **head** of the deque, so it behaves like a stack: last in, first out.

items.title: computeIfAbsent
items.prompt: In one statement, add `item` to the list stored under `key` in `Map<String, List<String>> groups`, creating a new `ArrayList` when the key is missing. Use `computeIfAbsent`.
items.explanation: `computeIfAbsent` returns the existing value, or creates, stores and returns a new one, so `.add` can follow directly.

items.title: filter, map, toList
items.prompt: From `List<String> names`, build `List<String> result` with the names longer than 3 characters, in upper case, using one stream ending in `toList()`.
items.explanation: `filter` keeps matching elements, `map` transforms them, and `toList()` (Java 16+) collects into an unmodifiable list.

items.title: groupingBy with counting
items.prompt: Build `Map<Integer, Long> byLength` that groups `List<String> words` by length and counts each group.
solutions:
Map<Integer, Long> byLength = words.stream()
    .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(w -> w.length(), Collectors.counting()));
items.explanation: The classifier gives the key and the downstream collector the value; `counting()` yields a `Long`.

items.title: reduce
items.prompt: Compute `int product` of `List<Integer> nums` with `reduce`, using the identity `1`.
solutions: int product = nums.stream().reduce(1, (a, b) -> a * b);
items.explanation: With an identity, `reduce` returns a plain value (not an `Optional`), and the identity is the result for an empty stream.

items.title: partitioningBy
items.prompt: Build `Map<Boolean, List<Integer>> parts` that splits `nums` into even (`true`) and odd (`false`) numbers.
items.explanation: `partitioningBy` always produces both keys, `false` and `true`, even when one list is empty.

items.title: BiFunction lambda
items.prompt: Declare `BiFunction<Integer, Integer, Integer> max` as a lambda that returns the larger argument using the conditional operator `? :`.
solutions: BiFunction<Integer, Integer, Integer> max = (a, b) -> a > b ? a : b;
BiFunction<Integer, Integer, Integer> max = (a, b) -> a >= b ? a : b;
items.explanation: A `BiFunction<T, U, R>` takes two arguments and returns an `R`. A single-expression lambda needs no braces or `return`.

items.title: Constructor reference
items.prompt: Declare `Supplier<List<String>> maker` as a constructor reference that creates a new `ArrayList`.
items.explanation: `ArrayList::new` is short for `() -> new ArrayList<>()`; each `get()` makes a new list.

items.title: joining
items.prompt: Join `List<String> parts` into `String csv`, separated by `, ` and wrapped in `[` and `]`, with the three-argument `Collectors.joining`.
items.explanation: `joining(delimiter, prefix, suffix)` adds the prefix and suffix once, around the whole result.

items.title: Virtual thread
items.prompt: Start a virtual thread that prints `working`, keep it in `Thread t`, and wait for it to finish.
items.explanation: `Thread.ofVirtual().start(task)` and `Thread.startVirtualThread(task)` both create and start a virtual thread. `join()` waits for it (and throws `InterruptedException`).

items.title: Callable and Future
items.prompt: In a try-with-resources, create `ExecutorService pool` with `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()`, submit a task returning `6 * 7` into `Future<Integer> f`, and print `f.get()`.
items.explanation: A lambda that returns a value is a `Callable`, so `submit` returns a `Future` of that type. `ExecutorService` is `AutoCloseable` since Java 19.

items.title: Lock idiom
items.prompt: Inside `increment()`, add one to `count` while holding `lock` (a `ReentrantLock`). Release the lock in a `finally` block.
items.explanation: Call `lock()` **before** the `try`: if it were inside and failed, `finally` would unlock a lock you don't hold.

items.title: synchronized method
items.prompt: In class `Counter` (field `int total`), write a `synchronized` instance method `void add(int n)` that adds `n` to `total`.
items.explanation: A synchronized instance method locks `this`, so only one thread at a time runs it on the same object.

items.title: Atomic update in a ConcurrentHashMap
items.prompt: Inside a parallel `forEach`, increment the count for `word` in `ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> counts` atomically with `merge`.
items.explanation: `ConcurrentHashMap.merge` is atomic per key. A `get` followed by `put` would lose updates under contention.

items.title: try-with-resources over a BufferedReader
items.prompt: Open `Path path` with `Files.newBufferedReader` in try-with-resources and print every line with a `readLine()` loop. `main` already `throws IOException`.
items.explanation: `readLine()` returns `null` at the end of the file, so assign and test in one expression. The reader is closed automatically, even when an exception is thrown.

items.title: Write and read a file
items.prompt: Write the text `"x\ny"` to `Path file` with `Files.writeString`, then read it back into `List<String> lines` with `Files.readAllLines`.
items.explanation: `writeString` creates or truncates the file (UTF-8 by default); `readAllLines` reads it fully into a list, splitting at line breaks.

items.title: normalize
items.prompt: Declare `Path p` for `/a/b/../c`, normalized, in one statement.
items.explanation: `normalize()` removes `.` and `name/..` pairs without touching the file system. `Path.of` (Java 11+) and `Paths.get` are equivalent.

items.title: Serializable with transient
items.prompt: Declare `class Session` that can be serialized, with a `String user` field and a `transient String token` field.
items.explanation: Implementing `Serializable` is enough to serialize; `transient` fields are skipped and come back as their default value (`null`).

items.title: Files.list in try-with-resources
items.prompt: Declare `long count` and set it to the number of regular files directly inside `Path dir`. Close the stream from `Files.list` with try-with-resources.
items.explanation: `Files.list` and `Files.walk` keep a directory handle open, so their streams should be closed. `Files.list` isn't recursive.

items.title: Adding days
items.prompt: Declare `LocalDate due` as 30 days after `LocalDate start`.
items.explanation: `LocalDate` is immutable, so `plusDays` returns a new date; keep the result.

items.title: Period between dates
items.prompt: Declare `Period age` as the period from `LocalDate birth` to `LocalDate today`.
items.explanation: `Period.between(start, end)` counts whole years, months and days; the end date is exclusive.

items.title: Formatting a date
items.prompt: Format `LocalDate d` as day/month/year with two-digit day and month (like `09/03/2024`) into `String s`.
items.explanation: `MM` is the month and `mm` the minute; `dd` is the day of the month and `DD` the day of the year.

items.title: Locale-specific numbers
items.prompt: Format `double amount` for `Locale.GERMANY` with `NumberFormat.getInstance` into `String text`.
items.explanation: German formatting uses `.` for grouping and `,` for decimals. The default `NumberFormat` shows up to three fraction digits.

items.title: Time zones
items.prompt: `LocalDateTime meeting` is Paris time. Declare `ZonedDateTime tokyo`: the same instant in `Asia/Tokyo`.
items.explanation: `atZone` attaches a zone to a local date-time; `withZoneSameInstant` converts to another zone, while `withZoneSameLocal` would keep the wall-clock time.

items.title: Creating a Locale
items.prompt: Declare `Locale swiss` for French as spoken in Switzerland (`fr`, `CH`) with the Java 19+ factory method.
items.explanation: `Locale.of(language, country)` replaces the deprecated `Locale` constructors. Language codes are lower case, country codes upper case.

items.title: module-info basics
items.prompt: Write `module-info.java` for module `com.shop.app`: it reads module `com.shop.api` and makes its own package `com.shop.app` available to other modules.
items.explanation: `requires` takes a module name; `exports` takes a package of this module. `java.base` is read implicitly.

items.title: Providing a service
items.prompt: Write `module-info.java` for `com.pay.card`: it reads `com.pay.api` and provides the service `com.pay.api.Payment` with the class `com.pay.card.Card`.
items.explanation: `provides <interface> with <implementation>` registers the provider; the consumer declares `uses <interface>`. The provider's package doesn't need to be exported.

items.title: requires transitive, qualified exports
items.prompt: Write `module-info.java` for `com.lib.util`: every module that reads it must also read `com.lib.core`, and its package `com.lib.util` is exported **only** to module `com.app`.
items.explanation: `requires transitive` gives readers of this module implied readability of `com.lib.core`. `exports ... to` is a qualified export, visible only to the listed modules.

items.title: opens for reflection
items.prompt: Write `module-info.java` for `com.data` that exports nothing but allows deep reflection on its package `com.data`, using an `opens` directive.
items.explanation: `opens` grants run-time reflective access (including private members) but no compile-time access. `open module` would open every package.

items.title: javac in module mode
items.prompt: Write one `javac` command that compiles module `com.app`, whose sources are in `src/com.app`, into the directory `out`, using the module source path.
items.explanation: `--module-source-path src` expects one folder per module (`src/com.app/...`); `-m` (`--module`) names the modules to compile and `-d` the output folder, which gets one subfolder per module.

items.title: Executable jar
items.prompt: The compiled classes are in `classes`. Write one `jar` command that creates `app.jar` from them with `com.app.Main` as the entry point.
items.explanation: `--main-class` (`-e`) writes `Main-Class` into the manifest so `java -jar app.jar` can run it, and `-C classes .` adds everything under `classes` without the `classes/` prefix.

items.title: Custom runtime image
items.prompt: Module `com.app` is compiled in `out`. Write one `jlink` command that builds a runtime image in folder `image` containing `com.app` and what it needs.
items.explanation: `jlink` links the root modules from `--add-modules` and everything they require into a minimal JRE at `--output`. The JDK's own modules are found automatically.
